note: Endpoints this app serves that the pack's agent API (agent_api/endpoints.json) does not have yet. tools/export_mcp_catalog.py adds them to the tool catalog, endpoints.md and the OpenAPI file. When the pack gets the same route, delete its entry here so the pack's own is used.

endpoints.description: The overlay library: `items` (clips to overlay, each with `id`, `category`, `duration`, size and `suggested_blend`), `fonts` (names a text clip's `font` can use: the bundled fonts, font files in the fonts folder and the fonts installed on the computer), `luts` (installed .cube files for a LUT clip), `caption_styles` (clean, bold, lower) and `kinds` (media, grain, vignette, text, lut). The person fills the library in the app (Post Process, Overlays). Use an item's `id` with POST /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers/media.

The project's overlays as the render sees it: `overlay_layer_track` (`enabled`), `overlay_layers` (every setting filled in and clamped), `count`, `revision`, and `warnings` for layers that will not draw as asked (a missing media file, a LUT or font that is not installed, an unknown kind, empty text). Overlays are drawn onto the final video by the stitch (`stitch_final`, `pipeline_build_full_video`) and by the Video Builder's Render All and Export. The timeline is in seconds from the start of the song.

Replace the project's overlays (`overlay_layers`, the whole list) and/or the switch for all of them (`overlay_layer_track`, `{"enabled": false}` turns every overlay off for every render without deleting the layers). Read first (GET), change what you need, send the list back. Later layers draw on top. Every layer has `kind` (media, grain, vignette, text, lut), `id`, `start` and `end` in seconds, `enabled`, `locked`, `opacity` (0 to 1), `fade_in` and `fade_out` (seconds). media: `path` (a file in the project, `overlay/<name>`, from POST /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers/media), `blend_mode` (screen drops black and suits dust, smoke and flares, then add, lighten, darken, overlay, softlight, hardlight, colordodge, colorburn, multiply, normal), `scale` (cover, contain, stretch), `loop`, `speed` (0.5 to 2), `flip_h`, `brightness` (-1 to 1), `contrast` (0 to 2), `tint` (#rrggbb). grain: `strength` (0 to 60, 20 to 30 is film), `chroma` (0 to 20), `size` (fine, medium, coarse), `animated`. vignette: `strength` (0 to 1, 0.7 is the default). text: `text`, `font`, `size` (pixels on a 1080 tall picture), `color`, `outline_width`, `outline_color`, `shadow`, `x` and `y` (0 to 1, the centre of the text), `animation` (none or slide_up). lut: `lut` (an installed .cube name), `strength` (0 to 1). Values out of range are clamped and the reply shows what was saved. A clip sent without `locked` is unlocked. Send If-Match with the revision you read.

Add `layers` (a list of overlay layers, fields as in PUT /projects/{pid}/overlay-layers) to the end of the list without touching the others. The reply is the whole list with `added`, the ids the new layers got.

Add one text clip for each lyric line, timed to the words of the song when the project has word timing (`project_context/timestamped_lyrics.json`, from the lyrics alignment) and otherwise one caption over each scene that has lyrics. `style` is clean (default), bold or lower (a lower third). `font` is a name from the library's `fonts` list and replaces the font of the style. `from` and `to` (seconds) limit it to a range. Captions from an earlier run are replaced (only those inside the range when one is given) unless `replace` is false. The reply is the whole list with `source` (timestamped_lyrics or scenes), `style` and `captions`.

Add a clip of the overlay library (`library_id`, from GET /overlay-library) as an overlay: it is copied into the project's `overlay` folder and starts at `start` (default 0) and runs to `end` (default the end of the timeline, looping its file). The blend mode is the library's suggestion (screen for clips on black). Any other media clip field (opacity, blend_mode, speed, fades) can be sent too. The reply is the whole list with `added` and the project `path`.

The transitions the timeline's transition lane can hold: `transitions` (each with `id`, `origin` (`original` for the app's own, `library` for the gl-transitions collection), `author`, `license`, `description`, `tags` and `params`: name, type, default and range of each setting), and `count`. Use an `id` as `transition` in the project's transitions or in a stitch.

The project's transitions in timeline order, as the stitch reads them: `scene_transitions`, each `{id, transition, start, end, seconds, params}` (a block of the timeline like an overlay: `start` and `end` are seconds on the timeline, `seconds` its length), `count`, and `revision`. On a cut between two scenes the block draws one scene into the other, inside a scene it is an effect on that scene's footage. Every stitch draws them, and so do the Video Builder's Render All and Export.

Replace all the project's transitions with `scene_transitions`, a list of `{transition, start, seconds, params, id}`. `transition` is an id from GET /transitions, `start` the time on the timeline in seconds, `seconds` the length 0.1 to 10 (default 0.5), `params` the settings to change from their defaults, `id` optional. Instead of `start`, `after_scene` (the number, 1 = first, or id of the scene before a cut) with `align` (center by default, end or start) puts the block on that cut. Blocks may not overlap: a later one starts where the one before it ends when the video is drawn. The reply is the saved list.

Add one transition, change one, or remove one, and leave the others alone. Without an `id` a new block is added at `start`, or on the cut after `after_scene` (placed around the cut by `align`). With the `id` of an existing block only the fields sent change. A `transition` that is null, empty or `none` removes the block with that `id`, or the blocks that cover the cut after `after_scene`. `seconds` and `params` are as in PUT /projects/{pid}/transitions. The reply is the whole list.

The effects the timeline's effect lane can hold: `effects` (each with `id`, `kind`, `category` (how the picker groups it), `origin` (`original`: the app's own), `author`, `license`, `description`, `tags` and `params`: name, type, default and range of each setting), and `count`. Use an `id` as `look` in the project's effects or in a stitch. An effect adds or bends something (a glitch, a blur, a flash). `progress` runs 0 to 1 over its block and `time` is the seconds since it started.

The project's effects in timeline order, as the stitch reads them: `video_effects`, each `{id, look, start, end, seconds, intensity, params}` (a block of the timeline like an overlay: `start` and `end` are seconds on the timeline, `seconds` its length, `intensity` 0 to 1 how much of its change is mixed in, `params` the settings changed from their defaults), `count`, and `revision`. Blocks may overlap: a frame gets every filter that covers it, then every effect. Every stitch draws them, and so do the Video Builder's Render All and Export, before the overlays are laid over the video.

Replace all the project's effects with `video_effects`, a list of `{look, start, seconds, intensity, params, id}`. `look` is an id from GET /effects, `start` the time on the timeline in seconds, `seconds` the length 0.05 or more (default 1), `intensity` 0 to 1 (default 1), `params` the settings to change from their defaults, `id` optional. The reply is the saved list.

Add one effect, change one, or remove one, and leave the others alone. Without an `id` a new block is added at `start`. With the `id` of an existing block only the fields sent change. A `look` that is null, empty or `none` removes the block with that `id`. `seconds`, `intensity` and `params` are as in PUT /projects/{pid}/effects. The reply is the whole list.

The filters the timeline's filter lane can hold: `filters` (each with `id`, `kind`, `category` (how the picker groups it), `origin` (`original`: the app's own), `author`, `license`, `description`, `tags` and `params`: name, type, default and range of each setting), and `count`. Use an `id` as `look` in the project's filters or in a stitch. A filter grades the colours: its settings are exposure, contrast, saturation, temperature, tint, highlights, shadows, fade, gamma, a split tone, a mono mix, a vignette, grain and sharpen. `Adjust` has every setting at its neutral value.

The project's filters in timeline order, as the stitch reads them: `video_filters`, each `{id, look, start, end, seconds, intensity, params}` (a block of the timeline like an overlay: `start` and `end` are seconds on the timeline, `seconds` its length, `intensity` 0 to 1 how much of its change is mixed in, `params` the settings changed from their defaults), `count`, and `revision`. Blocks may overlap: a frame gets every filter that covers it, then every effect. Every stitch draws them, and so do the Video Builder's Render All and Export, before the overlays are laid over the video.

Replace all the project's filters with `video_filters`, a list of `{look, start, seconds, intensity, params, id}`. `look` is an id from GET /filters, `start` the time on the timeline in seconds, `seconds` the length 0.05 or more (default 1), `intensity` 0 to 1 (default 1), `params` the settings to change from their defaults, `id` optional. The reply is the saved list.

Add one filter, change one, or remove one, and leave the others alone. Without an `id` a new block is added at `start`. With the `id` of an existing block only the fields sent change. A `look` that is null, empty or `none` removes the block with that `id`. `seconds`, `intensity` and `params` are as in PUT /projects/{pid}/filters. The reply is the whole list.
